title: Encode IRC §32(d)(2)(B) separated-spouse rule; replace the opaque satisfies_eitc_separated_spouse_rules input

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

body:
## Encoding debt

`us/statutes/26/32.yaml` rule `eitc_demographic_eligible` already has the post-2021 shape of §32(d):

```
filing_status == 1 or not taxpayer_married_under_general_rule or satisfies_eitc_separated_spouse_rules
```

The middle term is §7703(a), via `us:statutes/26/7703#taxpayer_married_under_general_rule`. But the §32(d)(2)(B) separated-spouse exception is the opaque leaf input `satisfies_eitc_separated_spouse_rules`, so the one condition that decides whether a married-filing-separately return can claim the EITC is asserted rather than encoded. Every version also starts at 2026-01-01, although the rule applies from TY2021.

This matters for adjudication. PolicyEngine-US grants the EITC to every separate filer from 2021, and TAXSIM gives childless separate filers the credit in 2021 only. The statute gives neither result.

## Statute (verbatim; extracted mechanically, independently re-verified)

26 U.S.C. §32(d), current text. Identical, apart from typography, on uscode.house.gov (prelim), Cornell LII, and the pinned corpus rows `us/statute/26/32/d`, `/d/1` and `/d/2` (release `us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap`):

> **(1) In general** In the case of an individual who is married, this section shall apply only if a joint return is filed for the taxable year under section 6013.
> **(2) Determination of marital status** For purposes of this section— **(A) In general** Except as provided in subparagraph (B), marital status shall be determined under section 7703(a). **(B) Special rule for separated spouse** An individual shall not be treated as married if such individual— (i) is married (as determined under section 7703(a)) and does not file a joint return for the taxable year, (ii) resides with a qualifying child of the individual for more than one-half of such taxable year, and (iii)(I) during the last 6 months of such taxable year, does not have the same principal place of abode as the individual’s spouse, or (II) has a decree, instrument, or agreement (other than a decree of divorce) described in section 121(d)(3)(C) with respect to the individual’s spouse and is not a member of the same household with the individual’s spouse by the end of the taxable year.

The effective date comes from the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, §9623(c): enrolled H.R. 1319, PDF pages 150–151; Pub. L. 117–2, 135 Stat. 154.

> (c) Effective Date.--The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2020.

The pre-2021 text (U.S. Code 2020 edition, §32(d)) was:

> In the case of an individual who is married (within the meaning of section 7703), this section shall apply only if a joint return is filed for the taxable year under section 6013.

It incorporated all of §7703, including §7703(b), and had no (d)(2).

§32(n), the 2021-only childless rules, contains no marital-status or filing-status rule. I extracted the full subsection and got zero hits for married, separate, 7703, joint, spouse and 6013.

## Why this is not a PR

- **Signed encoder only.** Content must come from `targeted-signed-reencode.yml`, carrying a v5 manifest from the protected signer.
- **The encoder pin must match.** rulespec-us CI requires each model manifest's `validation_execution.axiom_encode` to match the pinned encoder (`f856cfcb`, 0.2.2006). The failure reads "does not match the running pinned encoder". The workflow signs with axiom-encode main (0.2.2047 after axiom-encode#1699), so a dispatch has to ride the next encoder pin advance.
- **`32.yaml` is waiver-frozen** (`validate_failures`).
- **A full §32 re-encode is blocked** behind #1312 → axiom-encode#1665 → encoder pin → repoint → #1363. It also failed the complete-source-unit contract 4/4 on 2026-09-15 (run 34990688144).

## Plan

**Step 1. Encode a new module** for corpus citation `us/statute/26/32/d`. This follows the subsection-module precedent of `us/statutes/7/2015/f`, and the citation has no prior targeted runs. Dispatch it in the same wave as the next encoder pin advance, with `rulespec_ref`, `corpus_ref` and `rules_engine_ref` refreshed at that time. Paste this as `review_finding`:

> Encode 26 USC 32(d) (corpus us/statute/26/32/d, /d/1, /d/2) as its own module at us/statutes/26/32/d.yaml. us/statutes/26/32.yaml currently carries (d)(2)(B) as the opaque leaf input `satisfies_eitc_separated_spouse_rules`. This module must state the separated-spouse rule from its statutory elements so that 32.yaml can import it later. Do not import us:statutes/26/32, because 32.yaml will import this module.
>
> Required outputs, each with verbatim proof excerpts from the corpus provision:
> 1. A Judgment for (d)(2)(B), "shall not be treated as married". It holds only if all of:
>    - (i) the individual is married as determined under section 7703(a) (import us:statutes/26/7703#taxpayer_married_under_general_rule) and does not file a joint return for the taxable year;
>    - (ii) the individual resides with a qualifying child of the individual (section 32(c)(3)) for more than one-half of the taxable year (a leaf input stating exactly that);
>    - (iii) either (I) during the last 6 months of the taxable year the individual does not have the same principal place of abode as the spouse (leaf input), or (II) the individual has a decree, instrument, or agreement, other than a decree of divorce, described in section 121(d)(3)(C) with respect to the spouse (leaf input) AND is not a member of the same household with the spouse by the end of the taxable year (leaf input).
> 2. A Judgment for (d)(2)(A)+(B), "treated as married for purposes of section 32".
> 3. A Judgment for (d)(1): not treated as married, or a joint return is filed under section 6013 (consistent with 32.yaml's `filing_status == 1`).
>
> Pub. L. 117-2 §9623(c) makes the text effective for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2020. Use effective_from 2021-01-01 if validation accepts it with the 2026-only 7703 import; otherwise use 2026-01-01 and state the 2021 applicability in the summary.
>
> Companion tests, TY2026, each assigning every local input and the 7703 inputs:
> - A. Married, separate return, no qualifying child: (B) not_holds, (d)(1) not_holds.
> - B. Married, separate return, qualifying child, no shared abode in the last 6 months: (B) holds, (d)(1) holds.
> - C. Married, separate return, qualifying child, shared abode, no instrument: (B) not_holds, (d)(1) not_holds.
> - D. Joint return: (d)(1) holds.
> - E. Separate return, qualifying child, shared abode, written separation agreement, separate households at year end: (B) holds.
> - F. As E, but the same household at year end: (B) not_holds.
> - G. Legally separated under a decree of separate maintenance: not married, (d)(1) holds.

**Step 2. Declare pending oracle coverage.** Run `axiom-encode oracle-coverage-pending sync` for the new outputs (precedent: #1381). PE-US has no matching variable.

**Step 3. Re-encode §32.** In the post-repoint §32 re-encode, pass `existing_signed_imports_json=["us/statutes/26/32/d.yaml"]`, replace `satisfies_eitc_separated_spouse_rules` with the imported judgment, and retire the `validate_failures` waiver in the same change.

**Step 4. Add historical versions.** 2021–2025 need those years' EITC Rev. Proc. tables and §7703 versions before any pre-2026 case can be computed.

The full evidence (sources, sha256 checksums, pre/post diff, independent verification) and the engine comparison are in the local run folder `~/TheAxiomFoundation/_axiom-runs/irc-32d-2026-09-24/` (`EVIDENCE.md`, `ADJUDICATION.md`, `DISPATCH.md`).
